title: Redo role-prompt goal preservation; fix wrapping and stale 1,800 mention
summary: Redo the rejected job from the base: edit reader, producer and verifier prompts so a request's real goal survives to the verdict, make a non-empty request_reading_mismatch a Major finding in judge(), and raise the reader budget minimally. Fix the previous rejection's faults: keep rewritten doc lines at the file's wrap width, keep review-1 measurements purely past, and avoid the unclear "it" in verifier.md.

defaults_applied.how: The judge() change and its tests are Rust.
Unit tests cover mismatch present and absent; fmt, clippy and test must pass.
Docs and decision records are written for an outside reader.
The new budget is recorded with its measured count.
Every 1,800 mention is swept, not only the instance that surfaced.
The budget is raised only as far as needed.
Behavior criteria name the commands to run.
The earlier findings are recovered as criteria from the job record.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Audience of the prompt change: the later Athena roles (producer, verifier) and the user who judges the verdict.
The earlier verifier findings are mandatory criteria: no newly added doc line of 125 or more characters, no current budget in dated review-1 measurements, and no ambiguous pronoun in verifier.md.
Past-tense review and history records (docs/design/reviews/*, decisions.md:1971 history) may keep 1,800; present-tense statements get the new budget.
The self-check machinery proposed in the introspection is a separate job and is not part of this change.

acceptance_criteria.text: reader.md tells the reader to name the request's audience (who will use or judge the result) in the summary or assumptions.
reader.md requires at least one acceptance criterion written as an outcome the named audience can check; presence checks alone do not satisfy it.
reader.md forbids putting the request's own stated goal in out_of_scope, and tells the reader to read the current output the request is about before planning a change to it.
producer.md treats the acceptance criteria as a floor and tells the producer to serve the request's goal, while keeping the small-change and follow-conventions instructions.

verifier.md tells the verifier to judge user-facing output as its intended audience would, and to rate a request-reading mismatch at least major, never minor because the criteria passed. Its sentences have clear referents (for example, it names Athena where Athena ran the commands).

In judge() in crates/athena-core/src/verify.rs, a non-empty request_reading_mismatch adds a Major finding and a reason, so the verdict is not pass. Unit tests cover mismatch present and absent or blank. Run: cargo test -p athena-core verify
The BudgetSet::Reader budget is raised only as far as the new reader text needs. Run: cargo test --locked -p athena-cli --test budgets
docs/decisions.md records the new reader budget, the measured count, and why removals cannot pay for the new rules; CHANGELOG.md notes the change.

A repo-wide Grep for 1,800 and 1800 finds no present-tense statement of the old reader budget: defaults-loop.md:47, :227, :413; decision-sets.md:107, :111; decisions.md:612; athena-v0.md:1507, :1868; socratic-review.md:176, :198 if present tense, :219 are updated. Past-tense review records and history may keep it.
Grep for ^.{125,}$ on the edited docs finds no newly added line, including decision-sets.md around lines 107-114; rewrapped lines match the surrounding wrap width.
Dated review-1 measurements (decision-sets.md 'Measured (review 1...)' bullet and defaults-loop.md:227) remain purely past figures and do not mention the new budget.
The workspace stays clean and tested. Run: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, cargo test

out_of_scope: The pre-verification self-check, repair loop, and rejection-event changes proposed by the introspection.
Rewriting past-tense review records or history that cite the old 1,800 budget.
Changing other role prompts or the study capability's prompts beyond what the stated rules need.
Changes to athena.toml, defaults.toml, CI, or lint configuration.
departures: Many files and several sweep and wrap criteria, with two earlier rejections of the same job: the cost and time are higher than the reference, and verification is less likely to pass.
